manifest.name: dsh-wordcraft
manifest.description: WordCraft editor panel for DeepSeek Harness: live Word document editing next to the chat, synchronized with agent tool calls.

bundle.text:
# dsh-wordcraft: WordCraft editor panel for DeepSeek Harness.
#
# This bundle patch is applied after every bundle named in a profile's
# `dsh.profile.bundles`, in order. It inserts the skill provider and the stdio
# MCP server that fronts the bundled WordCraft editor runtime.
- insert:
    - id: wordcraft
      name: 'dsh-wordcraft'

    - id: mcp-wordcraft-wordcraft-editor
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      # Set DSH_MCP_WORDCRAFT=0 on the DSH process to run without the editor server.
      disabled: !!js "process.env.DSH_MCP_WORDCRAFT === '0'"
      config:
        serverName: wordcraft-editor
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 120000
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        # The adapter needs its package root to locate ui/bootstrap.mjs. Resolve
        # the installed package from the profile tree instead of hardcoding a path.
        cwd: !!js "(() => { const p = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path'); const req = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(baseUrl); return p.dirname(req.resolve('dsh-wordcraft/package.json')) })()"
        args:
          - !!js "process.getBuiltinModule('node:path').join((() => { const p = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path'); const req = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(baseUrl); return p.dirname(req.resolve('dsh-wordcraft/package.json')) })(), 'ui/bootstrap.mjs')"
        env:
          PLUGIN_ROOT: !!js "(() => { const p = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path'); const req = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(baseUrl); return p.dirname(req.resolve('dsh-wordcraft/package.json')) })()"
          PLUGIN_DATA: !!js "process.getBuiltinModule('node:path').join(process.getBuiltinModule('node:os').homedir(), '.dsh', 'plugin-data', 'dsh-wordcraft')"

readme.text:
**WordCraft editor panel for DeepSeek Harness** — open a real, editable Word document in DSH's right Sidebar Browser and watch the agent edit it live, in the same editor session.

> Unofficial community plugin. Not affiliated with DeepSeek or the WordCraft/ArtCraft teams.

- Registers one general `wordcraft-editor` skill for the parts an agent gets wrong unprompted: panel handoff and attachment, editor-session and cursor semantics, Word layout checks (sections, TOC/caption fields, tables, pagination) and save/verify rules. No scenario writing templates.
- Starts one stdio MCP server, `wordcraft-editor`, over a bundled WordCraft runtime — no download at first use.
- Serves the editor panel over a loopback HTTP URL with a random token. Click the link the agent prints: DSH opens it in the right Sidebar Browser.
- Keeps the panel and the agent on **one editor session**: `editor_status.attached` turns true once the page is loaded, and every `type_text` / `execute` call shows up in the panel immediately.

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0` (declared through `engines.dsh`).
- Node.js 24 or newer (the bundled editor runtime requires it).
- The right Sidebar Browser enabled in your Web profile (DSH ships it disabled for Web; see below).

From GitHub:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:lu123bing/dsh-wordcraft
```

Enable the right Sidebar Browser (one-time, in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: ui-sidebar-browser
  disabled: false
```

Restart DSH, then ask in a new session:

> 用 WordCraft 打开编辑器，帮我把这份周报整理成 DOCX。

The agent calls `open_browser_editor`, prints a `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<token>/` link, and waits until `editor_status` reports `attached: true` (usually 8–20 seconds). Click the link — the editor opens beside the chat and shares the agent's session.

If clicking the link opens a browser tab instead of the sidebar, set **Settings → General → link opening → In-App Sidebar**.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-wordcraft
```

Remove the `ui-sidebar-browser` entry again if you no longer want the browser panel.

1. `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the skill provider (`lib/index.js`) and one MCP client row (`wordcraft-editor` → `ui/bootstrap.mjs`).
2. `ui/bootstrap.mjs` verifies the bundled runtime against `ui/runtime.lock.json` (45 pinned files) and starts the editor adapter.
3. The adapter (`src/adapter.mjs`, bundled to `ui/dist/adapter.mjs`) exposes the editor's MCP tools and a loopback browser page. The panel talks to the adapter through the same MCP session the agent uses, which is why edits are shared rather than copied.
4. Every editor asset is served through chunked MCP resources (2 MiB per chunk); the panel runs as WebAssembly.

- One workspace per MCP instance: the first `open_editor` call binds the workspace; switching requires restarting DSH. Paths outside the workspace are rejected.
- The loopback page uses a random token and `Host`/`Origin` checks; no Node.js APIs are exposed to the page. The runtime is verified by SHA-256 before it runs and is never downloaded at runtime.
- The project bundles a pinned, prebuilt editor runtime; the panel UI has no network access (`connect-src 'none'`).
- Web sidebar iframes do not have the download permission: exports made inside the panel are written to `<workspace>/craft-exports/`; prefer `save_document` for deliverables.
- WordCraft's native CLI and the editor panel are separate sessions; save and reopen before switching.

```sh
npm install
npm run build:ui   # rebuild ui/dist/adapter.mjs and ui/dist/host.js from src/
npm test           # manifest, runtime lock, MCP handshake, source-cleanliness tests
```

The prebuilt WordCraft editor binary under `ui/dist/editor/` is a pinned artifact: run `node scripts/update-runtime-lock.mjs` after an intentional change and keep `ui/runtime.lock.json` in sync (`npm test` reports mismatches).

Apache-2.0 for this plugin's own code. The bundled WordCraft runtime and its automation overlay carry their own licenses and notices — see [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) and the complete third-party notices in [`ui/dist/editor/licenses/`](ui/dist/editor/licenses/).

The modified editor build follows the WordCraft brand license: product, community and brand references were removed or replaced, while copyright attribution and every upstream license/notice file are retained.
